newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland police probe public IRA display.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland police probe public IRA display.

text.p: Northern Ireland police were investigating an incident in which two armed and hooded IRA guerrillas appeared at a rally in Belfast and were described as defenders of the minority Roman Catholic community.

Police said the incident occurred on Tuesday at a North Belfast rally commemorating the 1916 uprising against British rule in Dublin. The uprising gave birth to the Irish Republican Army (IRA), which is fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland.
Witnesses said two men in balaclavas appeared from an alley while the crowd was being read a message from IRA prisoners held at the maximum-security Maze prison near Belfast.
They said the two IRA men were described by a rally organiser as "the men that are protecting our community... the only protection we have in the district".
One of the armed men had an AK-47 assault rifle, the guerrillas' habitual weapon, while the other had an Uzi submachine gun.

The incident was seen by security spokesmen as provocative in a tense period as the province braces itself for the outcome of a British general election on May 1 and the onset of the annual marching season by the majority Protestant community.

The IRA gained a foothold in the Catholic community 28 years ago when it cast itself as defenders of a faith it said was being persecuted by majority Protestants, who want the province to say British.
Northern Ireland's marching season got off to a peaceful start on Monday when Protestants voluntarily rerouted their parade to avoid passing through a Catholic section of Belfast.
But it coincided with an attempted bomb attack by Protestant Loyalist guerrillas on the Belfast offices of Sinn Fein, the political wing of the IRA.

The Loyalists, who want the province to stay British, said the attack was retaliation for a spate of IRA attacks in Britain and in Northern Ireland but they did not offically announce the end of their October 1994 ceasefire.
